verses.zh: 大卫对扫罗说完了话，约拿单的心与大卫的心深相契合。约拿单爱大卫，如同爱自己的性命。
verses.en: When David[NOTE:1] had finished talking with Saul, Jonathan and David became bound together in close friendship.[NOTE:2] Jonathan loved David as much as he did his own life.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the soul of Jonathan was bound with the soul of David.”
On the nature of Jonathan’s love for David, see J. A. Thompson, “The Significance of the Verb Love in the David-Jonathan Narratives in 1 Samuel,” VT 24 (1974): 334-38.tn Heb “like his [own] soul.”
verses.commentary:
18:1 "the soul of Jonathan was knit to the soul of David" This VERB (BDB 905, KB 1153,
Niphal PERFECT), "was knit," was used of Jacob and Benjamin in Gen. 44:30. This strong
bond of friendship is similar to Naomi and Ruth in Ruth 1:16-17.

▣ "soul. . .soul" The term nephesh (BDB 659) speaks of one's personhood or a physical life.
See full note online at Gen. 35:18 and Lev. 17:11.

▣ "Jonathan loved him as himself" In 1 Sam. 20:17 it says Jonathan loved David better than his own
life. In 2 Sam. 1:26 it says Jonathan loved David better than the love of a woman. Many have tried to interpret this as a
homosexual relationship but this is obviously an attempt to read modern presuppositions into an ancient text. David is
married in this chapter. This is just a metaphor for the deep friendship. The same idiom is used in Deut. 13:6.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOMOSEXUALITY

▣ "Jonathan" There are two forms of this name (BDB 220).

- 42 times ‒ יונתן

- 79 times ‒ יהונתן

verses.zh: 那日扫罗留住大卫，不容他再回父家。
verses.en: Saul retained David[NOTE:1] on that day and did not allow him to return to his father’s house.
notes: Heb “him”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 约拿单爱大卫如同爱自己的性命，就与他结盟。
verses.en: Jonathan made a covenant with David, for he loved him as much as he did his own life.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “like his [own] soul.”
verses.commentary:
18:3 "Then Jonathan made a covenant with David" This covenant involved not only friendship and faith but
apparently politics, cf. 1 Sam. 18:4; 23:17.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 约拿单从身上脱下外袍，给了大卫，又将战衣、刀、弓、腰带都给了他。
verses.en: Jonathan took off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with the rest of his gear including his sword, his bow, and even his belt.
verses.commentary:
18:4 "Jonathan stripped himself of the robe" This was probably a political symbol of the crown prince.

▣ "with his armor, including his sword and his bow and his belt" The magnitude of this gift can be
seen from the fact that Saul and Jonathan were the only members of the entire Israeli army that had weapons of
iron (cf. 1 Sam. 13:19,22).

verses.zh: 扫罗无论差遣大卫往何处去，他都做事精明。扫罗就立他作战士长，众百姓和扫罗的臣仆无不喜悦。
verses.en: On every mission on which Saul sent him, David achieved success. So Saul appointed him over the men of war. This pleased not only all the army, but also Saul’s servants.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “it was good in the eyes of all the people and also in the eyes of the servants of Saul.”
verses.commentary:
18:5 "So David went out wherever Saul sent him and prospered" David became very popular

- with the military

- with all the people

- in the sight of Saul's bureaucrats

verses.zh: 大卫打死了那非利士人，同众人回来的时候，妇女们从以色列各城里出来，欢欢喜喜，打鼓击磬，歌唱跳舞，迎接扫罗王。
verses.en: When the men[NOTE:1] arrived after David returned from striking down the Philistine, the women from all the cities of Israel came out singing and dancing to meet King Saul. They were happy as they played their tambourines and three-stringed instruments.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “them.” The masculine plural pronoun apparently refers to the returning soldiers.
Heb “with tambourines, with joy, and with three-stringed instruments.”
verses.commentary:
18:6 "the women came out of all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing" This was the common procedure for
greeting returning soldiers (cf. Exod. 15:20-21; Jdgs. 11:4; Ps. 68:25; 149:3).

▣ "musical instruments" The exact type of musical instrument is unknown (BDB 1026 II). The root of the
Hebrew word means "three," therefore, many have supposed that it was a triangle or three stringed instrument. This root
is used only here (NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 126).

verses.zh: 众妇女舞蹈唱和，说：「扫罗杀死千千，大卫杀死万万。」
verses.en: The women who were playing the music sang,“Saul has struck down his thousands,but David his tens of thousands!”
verses.commentary:
18:7 "Saul has slain his thousands,

And David his ten thousands" From this point on throughout the chapter, Saul's jealousy, immaturity,
and lack of self-worth can be easily seen.

Notice how the author describes Saul's motives.

- 1 Sam. 18:8 ‒ became very angry (jealousy)

- 1 Sam. 18:9 ‒ looked at David with suspicion (paranoia)

- 1 Sam. 18:10 ‒ an evil spirit. . .he raved

- 1 Sam. 18:11 ‒ murderous plan

- 1 Sam. 18:12 ‒ was afraid

- 1 Sam. 18:13 ‒ removed David from court

- 1 Sam. 18:15 ‒ dreaded David

- 1 Sam. 18:21 ‒ wanted his daughter to become a snare to David

- 1 Sam. 18:25 ‒ planned for David to be killed in battle by Philistines

- 1 Sam. 18:29 ‒ Saul was continually more afraid of David

In the MT, "thousand" is SINGULAR, but Masoretic scholars suggest the
PLURAL form.

verses.zh: 扫罗甚发怒，不喜悦这话，就说：「将万万归大卫，千千归我，只剩下王位没有给他了。」
verses.en: This made Saul very angry. The statement displeased him and he thought,[NOTE:1] “They have attributed to David tens of thousands, but to me they have attributed only thousands. What does he lack, except the kingdom?”
notes: Heb “said.” So also in vv. 11, 17.

verses.zh: 从这日起，扫罗就怒视大卫。
verses.en: So Saul was keeping an eye on David from that day onward.
verses.commentary:
18:9 "Saul looked at David with suspicion from that day on" Notice it is not David's actions, but other's
actions that caused Saul to begin to doubt David.

The VERB "looked" (BDB 745, KB 817, Qal PARTICIPLE) occurs
only here. BDB suggests a translation as "eye enviously" or "look askance," and KB "consider suspiciously."

verses.zh: 次日，从　神那里来的恶魔大大降在扫罗身上，他就在家中胡言乱语。大卫照常弹琴，扫罗手里拿着枪。
verses.en: The next day an evil spirit from God rushed upon Saul and he prophesied[NOTE:1] within his house. Now David was playing the lyre[NOTE:2] as usual. There was a spear in Saul’s hand,
notes: Or “he raved.” This same construction appears in 1 Sam 10:10 “the spirit of God rushed upon him and then he prophesied in their midst.” It is important to consider the agent affecting Saul, the verb describing his actions, and the broader cultural background. The phrase רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים (ruakh ʾelohim) could mean “a divine wind/spirit,” “a spirit from God,” or “the spirit of God.” Unlike 1 Sam 10:10, this case involves a harmful, or evil, spirit. The range of meaning of רָעָה (raʿah) can mean either harm or evil, and here indicates that this spirit’s purpose is to afflict Saul. The verb וַיִּתְנַבֵּא (vayyitnabbeʾ) is a Hitpael of the root נָבָא (nabaʾ) which means “to prophesy” in both the Niphal and the Hitpael. The difference may well be that the Niphal refers primarily to acting as a spokesman, while the Hitpael reflects an accompanying ecstatic experience on the part of the prophet (cf. 1 Sam 10:6; 19:24). 1 Kgs 18:29 also describes the antics of the prophets of Baal with the Hitpael of the root נָבָא (nabaʾ). Ecstatic experiences or expressions were sometimes associated with prophecy in the broader West Semitic culture as well as in the Israel. Some translations focus on the presumed outward effects of the afflicting spirit on Saul and render the verb “he raged” or “he raved” (NASB, ESV, NLT, NRSV). Although most biblical references to Israel’s prophets do not involve ecstatic experiences, the original audience would probably not have made a distinction here, that is, “raving” and “prophesying” would not have been considered alternatives.
The Hebrew text adds here “with his hand.”
verses.commentary:
18:10 "an evil spirit from God came upon Saul" This phrase occurs in 1 Sam. 16:13-14; 19:9; Isa. 45:7. See
Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 211-212 and see my full note at 1 Sam. 16:13.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS

▣ "raved" The root (BDB 612, KB 659, Hithpael IMPERFECT with waw)
is related to "prophet." The early prophets were an ecstatic group, cf. 1 Sam. 19:18-24. Raving was viewed
as a spiritual state.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHETS (OT)

▣ "a spear was in Saul's hand" This (BDB 333) was a symbol of his kingship (cf. 1 Sam. 22:6)

verses.zh: 扫罗把枪一抡，心里说，我要将大卫刺透，钉在墙上。大卫躲避他两次。
verses.en: and Saul threw the spear, thinking, “I’ll nail David to the wall!” But David escaped from him on two different occasions.
verses.commentary:
18:11 "I will pin David to the wall" Saul intended to kill David in vv. 10 and 11, 17,21,25; 19:9-10.

▣

NASB, NKJV
"escaped"

NRSV, NJB, JPSOA
"eluded"

TEV, REB
"dodged"

Peshitta
"evaded"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 685, KB 738, Qal IMPERFECT
with waw) which basically means "to turn about," so all of the English translations catch the thought.

Notice this kind of event happened twice. David was ministering to a mentally ill person, but remained!

verses.zh: 扫罗惧怕大卫；因为耶和华离开自己，与大卫同在。
verses.en: So Saul feared David, because the Lord was with David but had departed from Saul.
verses.commentary:
18:12 "for the Lord was with him" Saul knew YHWH had rejected him and
chosen another (cf. 1 Sam. 16:13,18). He clearly saw how David "prospered" (vv. 5,14). Saul knew "the
Lord was with David" (v. 28) but this caused even more fear and paranoia (v. 29).

This specific phrase is used of

- Abraham ‒ Gen. 21:22

- Jacob ‒ Gen. 28:15

- Samuel ‒ 1 Sam. 3:19

- David ‒ 1 Sam. 18:12,14; 2 Sam. 5:10

- Hezekiah ‒ 2 Kgs. 18:8

verses.zh: 所以扫罗使大卫离开自己，立他为千夫长，他就领兵出入。
verses.en: Saul removed David[NOTE:1] from his presence and made him a commanding officer.[NOTE:2] David led the army out to battle and back.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “him”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “an officer of a thousand.”
Heb “and he went out and came in before the people.” See v. 16.

verses.zh: 大卫做事无不精明，耶和华也与他同在。
verses.en: Now David achieved success in all he did,[NOTE:1] for the Lord was with him.
notes: Heb “in all his ways.”

verses.zh: 扫罗见大卫做事精明，就甚怕他。
verses.en: When Saul saw how very successful he was, he was afraid of him.

verses.zh: 但以色列和犹大众人都爱大卫，因为他领他们出入。
verses.en: But all Israel and Judah loved David, for he was the one leading them out to battle and back.

verses.zh: 扫罗对大卫说：「我将大女儿米拉给你为妻，只要你为我奋勇，为耶和华争战。」扫罗心里说：「我不好亲手害他，要藉非利士人的手害他。」
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Then Saul said to David, “Here’s my oldest daughter, Merab. I want to give her to you in marriage. Only be a brave warrior[NOTE:2] for me and fight the battles of the Lord.” For Saul thought, “There’s no need for me to raise my hand against him. Let it be the hand of the Philistines!”
notes: Much of the ms evidence for the LXX lacks vv. 17-19.
Heb “son of valor.”
verses.commentary:
18:17-19 "Then Saul said to David, 'Here is my older daughter'" Saul had promised to whoever fought and
defeated the Philistine giant he would give his daughter in marriage in 1 Sam. 17:25. However, David refused this offer in v. 18 because
he simply did not have the money to pay the dowry. We learn from this text that Saul was not doing this to fulfill his
promise but in order that the Philistines might kill David in battle.

18:17 "fight the Lord's battles" Notice that the enemies of Israel were the
enemies of YHWH. He was their "Divine Warrior." The battles were His (cf. Num. 21:14; 1 Sam. 18:17; 25:28).

verses.zh: 大卫对扫罗说：「我是谁，我是甚么出身，我父家在以色列中是何等的家，岂敢作王的女婿呢？」
verses.en: David said to Saul, “Who am I? Who are my relatives or the clan of my father[NOTE:1] in Israel that I should become the king’s son-in-law?”
notes: Heb “Who are my relatives, the clan of my father?” The term חַי (khay), traditionally understood as “my life,” is here a rare word meaning “family, kinfolk” (see HALOT 309 s.v. III חַי). The phrase “clan of my father” may be a scribal gloss explaining the referent of this rare word.
verses.commentary:
18:18

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta
"what is my life"

NRSV, REB, JPSOA footnote
"who are my kinsfolk"

NJB
"what is my lineage"

The MT has "what is my life" (BDB 311) but with a change of vocalization this can read, "who are my kin,"
which seems to fit the context better. The UBS Text Project supports the MT but suggests it is an ancient scribal error and
supports the conjecture of "my kinfolk," but without any MSS or ancient version support (see Gesenius'
Lexicon, p. 312b).

This same sense of family humility also characterized Saul at first (cf. 1 Sam. 9:21; 15:17).

verses.zh: 扫罗的女儿米拉到了当给大卫的时候，扫罗却给了米何拉人亚得列为妻。
verses.en: When the time came for Merab, Saul’s daughter, to be given to David, she instead was given in marriage to Adriel, who was from Meholah.
verses.commentary:
18:19 "she was given to Adriel the Meholathite" This man was from Gilead. Saul had a special
relationship with the men of this area (cf. 1 Samuel 11). This was a direct attempt to humiliate David.

verses.zh: 扫罗的次女米甲爱大卫。有人告诉扫罗，扫罗就喜悦。
verses.en: Now Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved David. When they told Saul about this, it[NOTE:1] pleased him.
notes: Heb “the matter.”
verses.commentary:
18:20 This is a surprising verse. Why was Saul pleased knowing his daughter loved David (cf. v. 28)?

- He saw it as a chance to manipulate David into a battle in which he would hopefully be killed (vv. 21,25).

- To marry the oldest daughter entitled one to a special title, "son-in-law of the king," but this title would not
go to the one who married a younger daughter.

The VERB (BDB 448, KB 449, Qal IMPERFECT with
waw) basically means "to be smooth," "to be straight," or "to be right." Here, it is an idiom for "pleasure"
(i.e., 1 Sam. 18:20,26; 2 Sam. 17:4; 1 Chr. 13:4; 2 Chr. 30:4).

verses.zh: 扫罗心里说：「我将这女儿给大卫，作他的网罗，好藉非利士人的手害他。」所以扫罗对大卫说：「你今日可以第二次作我的女婿。」
verses.en: Saul said, “I will give her to him so that she may become a snare to him and so the hand of the Philistines may be against him.” So Saul said to David, “Today is the second time for you to become my son-in-law.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The final sentence of v. 21 is absent in most LXX mss.
verses.commentary:
18:21 "For a second time you may be my son-in-law today" This seems to be related to v. 26, "before the
days had expired." There was apparently a time limit for David to provide a dowry and marry one of Saul's daughters
(v. 25). However, by changing one of the consonants in the Hebrew text, this phrase can mean "within two years."
Whatever the time limit imposed, it is obvious there was a time limit.

verses.zh: 扫罗吩咐臣仆说：「你们暗中对大卫说：『王喜悦你，王的臣仆也都喜爱你，所以你当作王的女婿。』」
verses.en: Then Saul instructed his servants, “Tell David secretly, ‘The king is pleased with you, and all his servants like you. So now become the king’s son-in-law.’”

verses.zh: 扫罗的臣仆就照这话说给大卫听。大卫说：「你们以为作王的女婿是一件小事吗？我是贫穷卑微的人。」
verses.en: So Saul’s servants spoke these words privately to[NOTE:1] David. David replied, “Is becoming the king’s son-in-law something insignificant to you? I’m just a poor and lightly esteemed man!”
notes: Heb “in the ears of.”

verses.zh: 扫罗的臣仆回奏说，大卫所说的如此如此。
verses.en: When Saul’s servants reported what David had said,

verses.zh: 扫罗说：「你们要对大卫这样说：『王不要甚么聘礼，只要一百非利士人的阳皮，好在王的仇敌身上报仇。』」扫罗的意思要使大卫丧在非利士人的手里。
verses.en: Saul replied, “Here is what you should say to David: ‘There is nothing that the king wants as a price for the bride except 100 Philistine foreskins, so that he can be avenged of his[NOTE:1] enemies.’” (Now Saul was thinking that he could kill David by the hand of the Philistines.)
notes: Heb “the king’s.”
verses.commentary:
18:25 "dowry" This is the Hebrew word "mohar" (BDB 555). It appears only three times in the OT
(cf. Gen. 34:12; Exod. 22:16; here) but it reflects the marriage custom of the ANE. The bride's father set the amount.
For a good brief discussion see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, "Typical Israelite Marriage," pp. 26-29
and NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 859-862.

The price could be

- money/weight of metals/valuables (the normal way)

- service (Gen. 29:20,27-28; Exod. 2:21)

- act of valor

- Caleb (Josh. 15:16-17; Jdgs. 1:12)

- David (1 Sam. 17:25; 18:20-27; 2 Sam. 3:14)

verses.zh: 扫罗的臣仆将这话告诉大卫，大卫就欢喜作王的女婿。日期还没有到，
verses.en: So his servants told David these things and David agreed[NOTE:1] to become the king’s son-in-law. Now the specified time had not yet expired[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and it was acceptable in the eyes of David.”
Heb “the days were not fulfilled.”

verses.zh: 大卫和跟随他的人起身前往，杀了二百非利士人，将阳皮满数交给王，为要作王的女婿。于是扫罗将女儿米甲给大卫为妻。
verses.en: when David, along with his men, went out[NOTE:1] and struck down 200 Philistine men. David brought their foreskins and presented all of them to the king so that he could become the king’s son-in-law. Saul then gave him his daughter Michal in marriage.
notes: Heb “arose and went.”
verses.commentary:
18:27 How would you liked to have beeen the person who extracted these "foreskins" from these dead
soldiers? This gesture was

- to prove the number of dead

- to prove they were Philistines

verses.zh: 扫罗见耶和华与大卫同在，又知道女儿米甲爱大卫，
verses.en: When Saul realized[NOTE:1] that the Lord was with David and that his[NOTE:2] daughter Michal loved David,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “saw and knew.”
Heb “Saul’s.” In the translation the proper name has been replaced by the pronoun for stylistic reasons.
Heb “him”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
18:28 This verse should have made Saul happy, but no, just the opposite (cf. v. 29).

The LXX (RSV) has "that all Israel loved him" (NJB). The UBS Text Project supports the
MT ("Saul's daughter loved him") with a "B" rating (some doubt).

verses.zh: 就更怕大卫，常作大卫的仇敌。
verses.en: Saul became even more afraid of him.[NOTE:1] Saul continued to be at odds with David from then on.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “of David.” In the translation the proper name has been replaced by the pronoun for stylistic reasons.
The final sentence of v. 29 is absent in most LXX mss.tn Heb “all the days.”

verses.zh: 每逢非利士军长出来打仗，大卫比扫罗的臣仆做事精明，因此他的名被人尊重。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The leaders of the Philistines would march out, and as often as they did so, David achieved more success than all of Saul’s servants. His name was held in high esteem.
notes: Verse 30 is absent in most LXX mss.
verses.commentary:
18:30 This is a summary statement of how everyone knew YHWH was with David. David's reputation grew!

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- The Philistines

- They were Aegean people probably from the island of Crete.

- They tried to invade Egypt around 1200 b.c. but were defeated and subsequently settled on the southwestern
coast of Palestine about the time of Joshua's invasion of the land.

- They were the only possessors in the area of Iron Age technology.

- They assimilated Canaanite culture instead of importing their own, therefore, there was a rapid degree of
settlement and stability.

- Saul's Problems

- Saul's problems begin when he disobeys and rebels against God.

- 1 Sam. 13:12-13, where he offered a sacrifice without waiting for Samuel

- 1 Sam. 15:20-23, where he did not fulfill God's orders in killing the Amalekites

- The rejection of Saul and the anointing of David at Bethlehem had already occurred by 1 Samuel 18.

- "The evil spirit of the Lord" is an OT understanding of only one God, one source
in the universe (cf. 1 Sam. 16:13-14; 19:9; Jdgs. 9:23; 2 Chr. 20:6; Eccl. 7:14; Isa. 14:24-27; 43:13; 15:7; 54:16;
Jer. 18:11; Lam. 3:33-38; Amos 3:6).

- Saul's personality problems can be seen in his changing attitudes toward David.

- love, 1 Sam. 16:21

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 18:1-5

1Now it came about when he had finished speaking to Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit
to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as himself. 2Saul took him that day and did not let
him return to his father's house. 3Then Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved
him as himself. 4Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was on him and gave it to David, with
his armor, including his sword and his bow and his belt. 5So David went out wherever Saul sent
him, and prospered; and Saul set him over the men of war. And it was pleasing in the sight of all the
people and also in the sight of Saul's servants.
